newsitem.title: CANADA: Imasco says profits on rise, outlook bright.
newsitem.headline: Imasco says profits on rise, outlook bright.

text.p: Imasco Ltd., Canada's biggest cigarette maker, said on Thursday it posted stronger profits in the final quarter of the year with growth from its tobacco and financial services units.
Imasco, whose Imperial Tobacco unit has a 67 percent share of the Canadian cigarette market, also said it was on track for another strong year in 1997.

Imasco reported a fourth-quarter profit of C$164 million ($121 million) or C70 cents (52 cents) a share, compared with a loss of C$177 million ($131 million) or C76 cents (56 cents) a share a year earlier.

The 1995 fourth quarter loss included a C$325 million ($241 million) charge related to the sale of the Roy Rogers restaurant outlets in the United States by Imasco's money-losing Hardee's Food Systems unit.
Imasco's fourth quarter 1996 sales were C$2.9 billion ($2.1 billion) compared with C$2.5 billion ($1.85 billion) a year earlier.

For the full 1996 year, Imasco had net earnings of C$601 million ($445 million) or C$2.55 ($1.90) a share, compared with C$221 million ($164 million) or C91 cents (67 cents) a share in 1995 after the special charge. Sales in 1996 were C$10.7 billion ($7.9 billion) vs. C$9.9 billion ($7.3 billion) in 1995.
Brian Levitt, president, said 1997 promised to be an "exciting" year of the company.
"On the operating front, Hardee's will continue to be a major challenge. However, each of Imasco's other businesses is on course for another strong performance in 1997," Levitt said.
Imperial Tobacco led other Imasco units in the latest fourth quarter with operating earnings of C$199 million ($147 million) compared with C$180 million ($133 million) a year earlier.

Operating earnings at CT Financial Services, which controls Canada Trust, a financial services company that is challenging Canada's big six national banks, rose 8 percent to C$125 million ($93 million) in the latest quarter.

Levitt said Imasco expected to record a large one-time gain from CT Financial's sale of its U.S. subsidiary, First Federal Savings and Loan Association of Rochester, a transaction which is expected to close in the current first quarter.
But the First Federal sale also would have a "dampening effect" on the parent company's earnings growth in 1997, he said.
On the Toronto Stock Exchange Thursday afternoon, Imasco shares closed 15 cents higher to end at C$36.15 ($26.78) in light trading.
